claim: Natural competence for transformation is a primary mode of horizontal gene transfer.
source: Natural competence for transformation is a primary mode of horizontal gene transfer.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about horizontal gene transfer mechanisms.

claim: Competent bacteria are able to absorb free DNA from their surroundings and exchange this DNA against pieces of their own genome when sufficiently homologous.
source: Competent bacteria are able to absorb free DNA from their surroundings and exchange this DNA against pieces of their own genome when sufficiently homologous.
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of natural competence.

claim: Naturally competent Vibrio cholerae use their type VI secretion system (T6SS) to actively acquire DNA from non-kin neighbors.
source: In this context, we previously showed that naturally competent Vibrio cholerae use their type VI secretion system (T6SS) to actively acquire DNA from non-kin neighbors.
evidence: The authors reference their previous work showing this mechanism.

claim: Competent V. cholerae acquire DNA fragments with a length exceeding 150 kbp in a T6SS-dependent manner.
source: We show that competent V. cholerae acquire DNA fragments with a length exceeding 150 kbp in a T6SS-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by whole-genome sequencing data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The environmental lifestyle of V. cholerae fosters the exchange of genetic material with sufficient coding capacity to significantly accelerate bacterial evolution.
source: Collectively, our data support the notion that the environmental lifestyle of V. cholerae fosters the exchange of genetic material with sufficient coding capacity to significantly accelerate bacterial evolution.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Vibrio cholerae is responsible for seven major pandemics since 1817, one of which is still ongoing.
source: The causative agent of the diarrheal disease cholera, Vibrio cholerae, is responsible for seven major pandemics since 1817, one of which is still ongoing.
evidence: This is established historical and epidemiological knowledge about cholera.

claim: Cholera affects between 1 and 4 million people and causes 21,000–143,000 deaths per year.
source: Due to its ability to rapidly spread in contaminated water, cholera poses a serious world health risk, affecting between 1 and 4 million people and causing 21,000–143,000 deaths per year, especially in poor or underdeveloped countries (WHO, 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to WHO 2019 data.

claim: V. cholerae acquire new phenotypes through horizontal gene transfer (HGT).
source: One way in which V. cholerae acquire new phenotypes is through horizontal gene transfer (HGT), which is the direct movement of DNA from one organism to another.
evidence: This is established knowledge about bacterial evolution mechanisms.

claim: Natural competence for transformation allows bacteria to absorb free DNA from their surroundings using their competence-induced DNA-uptake complex.
source: A major mode of HGT is natural competence for transformation in which bacteria are able to absorb free DNA from their surroundings using their competence-induced DNA-uptake complex (Chen and Dubnau, 2004; Johnston et al., 2014; Matthey and Blokesch, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: When sufficient homology is present between the incoming DNA and the bacterial genome, the absorbed genetic material can be integrated into the genome via double homologous recombination.
source: When sufficient homology is present between the incoming DNA and the bacterial genome, the absorbed genetic material can be integrated into the genome via double homologous recombination at the expense of the initial DNA region.
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of homologous recombination in transformation.

claim: V. cholerae gained an ~40 kbp O139-antigen cluster at the expense of the original ~30 kbp O1-antigen cluster through natural transformation.
source: As an example of the significant power of this natural competence for gene uptake, we previously witnessed the gain of an ~40 kbp O139-antigen cluster at the expense of the original ~30 kbp O1-antigen cluster through natural transformation (followed by strong selective pressure exerted by antibiotics or phages; Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2007), which significantly changed the phenotypes of these bacteria.
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: Griffith's experiment in 1928 unambiguously proved that transformation contributes to evolution and pathogen emergence.
source: And while Griffith's experiment in 1928 unambiguously proved that transformation contributes to evolution and pathogen emergence, the general prevalence of non-degraded DNA with sufficient coding capacity has been questioned (Nielsen et al., 2007; Overballe-Petersen et al., 2013; Croucher et al., 2016), drawing inquiries as to whether this mode of HGT could be responsible for the major changes causing pandemic strains to emerge.
evidence: This references the historical Griffith experiment and subsequent questioning in the literature.

claim: The induction of competence in V. cholerae is tightly regulated.
source: The induction of competence in V. cholerae is tightly regulated (recently reviewed by Metzger and Blokesch, 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: V. cholerae becomes naturally competent for genetic transformation upon growth on chitin-rich exoskeletons of zooplankton.
source: Briefly, upon growth on the (molted) chitin-rich exoskeletons of zooplankton (Pruzzo et al., 2008), the most abundant polysaccharide in the aquatic environment and therefore an important carbon source for chitinolytic bacteria (Gooday, 1990), the expression pattern of V. cholerae is altered (Meibom et al., 2004) to render it naturally competent for genetic transformation (Meibom et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Chitin is the most abundant polysaccharide in the aquatic environment.
source: Briefly, upon growth on the (molted) chitin-rich exoskeletons of zooplankton (Pruzzo et al., 2008), the most abundant polysaccharide in the aquatic environment and therefore an important carbon source for chitinolytic bacteria (Gooday, 1990), the expression pattern of V. cholerae is altered (Meibom et al., 2004) to render it naturally competent for genetic transformation (Meibom et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Gooday, 1990.

claim: When chitin degradation products are sensed by V. cholerae, it produces the regulatory protein TfoX.
source: Initially, when chitin degradation products are sensed by V. cholerae, it produces the regulatory protein TfoX (Li and Roseman, 2004; Meibom et al., 2004; Meibom et al., 2005; Yamamoto et al., 2011; Dalia et al., 2014; Yamamoto et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: TfoX positively regulates the expression of the major DNA-uptake machinery in V. cholerae.
source: This competence activator positively regulates the expression of the major DNA-uptake machinery in the cell (Matthey and Blokesch, 2016), providing a direct connection between growth on chitin and competence activation.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: HapR acts as repressor of dns, which encodes an extracellular nuclease that inhibits transformation.
source: Apart from TfoX, natural competence and transformation also depend on the master regulator of quorum sensing, HapR, in two ways: i) HapR acts as repressor of dns, which encodes an extracellular nuclease that inhibits transformation (Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2008); and ii) HapR together with TfoX co-activates the transcription factor QstR, which further represses dns as well as activates several DNA-uptake genes (Lo Scrudato and Blokesch, 2013; Jaskólska et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: HapR together with TfoX co-activates the transcription factor QstR.
source: Apart from TfoX, natural competence and transformation also depend on the master regulator of quorum sensing, HapR, in two ways: i) HapR acts as repressor of dns, which encodes an extracellular nuclease that inhibits transformation (Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2008); and ii) HapR together with TfoX co-activates the transcription factor QstR, which further represses dns as well as activates several DNA-uptake genes (Lo Scrudato and Blokesch, 2013; Jaskólska et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: QstR represses dns and activates several DNA-uptake genes.
source: Apart from TfoX, natural competence and transformation also depend on the master regulator of quorum sensing, HapR, in two ways: i) HapR acts as repressor of dns, which encodes an extracellular nuclease that inhibits transformation (Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2008); and ii) HapR together with TfoX co-activates the transcription factor QstR, which further represses dns as well as activates several DNA-uptake genes (Lo Scrudato and Blokesch, 2013; Jaskólska et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Environmental DNA is often heavily degraded and therefore short in size.
source: While the chitin-induced DNA-uptake complex of V. cholerae is able to absorb DNA from the surrounding (Seitz and Blokesch, 2013; Seitz and Blokesch, 2014; Seitz et al., 2014; Ellison et al., 2018; Adams et al., 2019), environmental DNA is often heavily degraded and therefore short in size (Nielsen et al., 2007; Overballe-Petersen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Free DNA is thought to originate from dead and therefore less fit bacteria.
source: In addition, free DNA is thought to originate from dead and therefore less fit bacteria, which renders the coding part of such genetic material non-favorable for naturally competent bacteria (Redfield, 1988).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Redfield, 1988.

claim: V. cholerae actively acquires 'fresh' DNA from healthy, living bacteria through kin-discriminatory neighbor predation.
source: In line with these arguments, we recently showed that V. cholerae does not solely rely on randomly released environmental DNA. Instead, it actively acquires 'fresh' DNA from healthy, living bacteria through kin-discriminatory neighbor predation (Borgeaud et al., 2015), which, conceptually, also occurs in other naturally competent bacteria (Veening and Blokesch, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research by the authors and others.

claim: Neighbor predation in V. cholerae is accomplished by a contractile injection system known as the type VI secretion system (T6SS) that transports toxic effector proteins into prey.
source: Neighbor predation in V. cholerae is accomplished by a contractile injection system known as the type VI secretion system (T6SS) that transports toxic effector proteins into prey (Ho et al., 2014; Cianfanelli et al., 2016; Galán and Waksman, 2018; Taylor et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The T6SS of pandemic V. cholerae is co-regulated with its DNA-uptake machinery in a TfoX-, HapR-, and QstR-dependent manner when the bacterium grows on chitin.
source: Intriguingly, the T6SS of pandemic V. cholerae is exquisitely co-regulated with its DNA-uptake machinery in a TfoX-, HapR-, and QstR-dependent manner when the bacterium grows on chitin (Borgeaud et al., 2015; Watve et al., 2015; Metzger et al., 2016; Jaskólska et al., 2018), which increases the chances of the competent bacterium to take up freshly released DNA compared to free-floating 'unfit' DNA.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: The coupling of competence and type VI secretion is conserved in several non-cholera vibrios.
source: Notably, this coupling of competence and type VI secretion is also conserved in several non-cholera vibrios (Metzger et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The WT predator strain efficiently absorbed and integrated the prey-released resistance cassettes (aph or cat).
source: As shown in Figure 1, the WT predator strain efficiently absorbed and integrated the prey-released resistance cassettes (aph or cat), while the transformation efficiency for the T6SS-defective acceptor strain was significantly reduced (by 97.8% and 99.2% for aph and cat, respectively) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The transformation efficiency for the T6SS-defective acceptor strain was significantly reduced by 97.8% and 99.2% for aph and cat, respectively.
source: As shown in Figure 1, the WT predator strain efficiently absorbed and integrated the prey-released resistance cassettes (aph or cat), while the transformation efficiency for the T6SS-defective acceptor strain was significantly reduced (by 97.8% and 99.2% for aph and cat, respectively) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Comparable frequencies were observed for both selective markers (aph and cat), suggesting that their acquisition does not significantly affect the strains' fitness under non-selective conditions.
source: Moreover, comparable frequencies were observed for both selective markers, suggesting that their acquisition does not significantly affect the strains' fitness under non-selective conditions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data showing similar transformation frequencies.

claim: The comEA-minus strain was never transformed under predator-prey co-culture conditions, confirming that the gene transfer depended entirely on natural competence.
source: We tested whether these transfer events were indeed competence-mediated and not based on other modes of HGT using a strain with a competence-related DNA import deficiency in that it lacked the competence protein ComEA that reels external DNA into the periplasm (Seitz et al., 2014). This comEA-minus strain was never transformed under these predator-prey co-culture conditions, confirming that the gene transfer did depend entirely on natural competence.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding that confirms the mechanism of gene transfer.

claim: Double-resistance acquisition occurred at lower rates compared to single-resistant clones and were mostly below the limit of detection for the T6SS-minus acceptor strain.
source: Next, we scored the frequencies of transformants that had adopted resistance against both antibiotics, which would show the possibility of two transformation events or the transfer of a large piece of DNA (indicated by the distance between the two genes on the same chromosome). These transformations occurred, as expected, at lower rates compared to single-resistant clones and were mostly below the limit of detection for the T6SS-minus acceptor strain (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A gradual decrease in the frequencies was observed the further the two resistance genes were apart from each other on the same chromosome.
source: Interestingly, we observed a gradual decrease in the frequencies the further the two resistance genes were apart from each other on the same chromosome, while a sharp drop occurred in the number of recovered transformants when the two resistance genes were carried on the two separate prey chromosomes (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: A sharp drop occurred in the number of recovered transformants when the two resistance genes were carried on the two separate prey chromosomes.
source: Interestingly, we observed a gradual decrease in the frequencies the further the two resistance genes were apart from each other on the same chromosome, while a sharp drop occurred in the number of recovered transformants when the two resistance genes were carried on the two separate prey chromosomes (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: When the two resistance genes are carried in trans, at least two separate DNA-uptake events are required.
source: While the latter scenario unambiguously requires at least two separate DNA-uptake events, the former, in which the resistance markers are carried in cis, could reflect a mix between single and multiple DNA absorption and integration events.
evidence: This is a logical inference about the mechanism of DNA uptake.

claim: When purified genomic DNA was provided, the in cis double-resistance acquisition efficiencies reached a comparable range to the in trans efficiencies when the two resistance genes were separated by at least 100 kbp.
source: When purified genomic DNA was instead provided as the transforming material to simplify the experiment and provide measurable results for all conditions, the in cis double-resistance acquisition efficiencies reached a comparable range to the in trans efficiencies when the two resistance genes were separated by at least 100 kbp.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the purified DNA experiments.

claim: Transformations of less than 100 kbp likely often occurred through a single acquisition.
source: This suggested that the more efficient transformations of less than 100 kbp likely often occurred through a single acquisition (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The WT predator and T6SS-minus acceptor behaved similarly when purified DNA was provided.
source: Furthermore, the WT predator and T6SS-minus acceptor behaved similarly when purified DNA was provided, which makes sense as the need for active DNA release through neighbor predation was eliminated.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding with an inference about the mechanism.

claim: Neighbor predation might foster the transfer of long DNA stretches, which frequently exceeded 50 kbp.
source: Based on these data and the fact that the double-acquisition rates for the T6SS-minus acceptor strain were mostly below the detection limit in the prey scenario (Figure 1B), we hypothesized that neighbor predation might foster the transfer of long DNA stretches, which frequently exceeded 50 kbp and therefore carry significant coding capacity.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental data.

claim: Long DNA stretches released from killed prey might saturate the system against uptake of additional fragments.
source: Moreover, the significantly lower double-acquisition rates when both cassettes are located in trans (e.g., on two different chromosomes) for the co-culturing conditions compared to the supplementation of purified gDNA (Figure 1—figure supplement 1) led us speculate that long DNA stretches might be released from the killed prey thereby saturating the system against uptake of additional fragments.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental data.

claim: A1552 is a pandemic O1 El Tor strain belonging to the LAT-1 sublineage of the West-African South American (WASA) lineage of seventh pandemic V. cholerae strains.
source: A1552 is a pandemic O1 El Tor strain (Yildiz and Schoolnik, 1998) belonging to the LAT-1 sublineage of the West-African South American (WASA) lineage of seventh pandemic V. cholerae strains (Domman et al., 2017) while strain Sa5Y was isolated from the Californian Coast (Keymer et al., 2007; Miller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: Strain Sa5Y was isolated from the Californian Coast.
source: A1552 is a pandemic O1 El Tor strain (Yildiz and Schoolnik, 1998) belonging to the LAT-1 sublineage of the West-African South American (WASA) lineage of seventh pandemic V. cholerae strains (Domman et al., 2017) while strain Sa5Y was isolated from the Californian Coast (Keymer et al., 2007; Miller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The environmental isolate Sa5Y lacked several genomic regions including VPI-1, VPI-2, VSP-I, VSP-II, the cholera toxin prophage CTX, and the WASA-1 element.
source: Indeed, as expected from its non-clinical origin, the environmental isolate lacked several genomic regions, including those that encode major virulence features, namely Vibrio pathogenicity islands 1 and 2 (VPI-1, VPI-2), Vibrio seventh pandemic islands I and II (VSP-I, VSP-II; Dziejman et al., 2005), the cholera toxin prophage CTX (Waldor and Mekalanos, 1996), and the WASA-1 element.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative genomics analysis presented in the study.

claim: The O-antigen cluster of Sa5Y differed significantly from the O1-encoding genes of pandemic strain A1552.
source: In addition, the strain's O-antigen cluster differed significantly from the O1-encoding genes of pandemic strain A1552 (Figure 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative genomics analysis shown in Figure 2.

claim: The integron island differed the most between strains A1552 and Sa5Y.
source: The region that differed the most between both strains was the integron island, which is consistent with the role of this assembly platform in fostering the incorporation of exogenous open reading frames (Mazel, 2006).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative genomics analysis with a citation supporting the interpretation.

claim: The overall SNP frequency between A1552 and Sa5Y is approximately 1 in 55 nucleotides for conserved genes.
source: Given these major differences between strain A1552 and Sa5Y and, in addition, an overall SNP frequency of approximately 1 in 55 nucleotides for conserved genes, we concluded that HGT events occurring between these two strains on chitinous surfaces could be precisely scored using short-read sequencing.
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative genomics analysis.

claim: The pandemic strains and Sa5Y contained nine or ten rRNA clusters in total compared to the initially reported eight.
source: Apart from this important genomic information, we also noted that the pandemic strains as well as Sa5Y contained previously unrecognized rRNA operons, with nine or ten rRNA clusters in total compared to the initially reported eight (Heidelberg et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a finding from the genomic analysis that corrects previous reports.

claim: Kanamycin-resistant transformants of A1552 were selected at an average frequency of 1.8 × 10−4 after 30 hr co-culturing on chitin.
source: Using this system, resistant transformants of A1552 were selected at an average frequency of 1.8 × 10−4 after the 30 hr co-culturing on chitin, and 20 of those transformants were randomly picked for further analysis.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from the co-culture experiments.

claim: The location and the size of the prey-donated genomic region differed significantly between most transformants.
source: As shown in Figure 3, apart from the common acquisition of the aph resistance cassette, the location and the size of the prey-donated genomic region differed significantly between most transformants.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 3.

claim: The average length of total acquired DNA was previously estimated to be ~23 kbp in experiments using purified donor gDNA.
source: Previous estimates of the average length of total acquired DNA were made in experiments using purified donor gDNA and were considered to be ~23 kbp (Miller et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a citation to previous research.

claim: The average length of the total acquired DNA in the current experiments was almost 70 kbp.
source: Importantly, we observed in these new experiments that the average length of the total acquired DNA, meaning the DNA surrounding the aph cassette plus any transferred regions elsewhere on either of the two chromosomes, was almost 70 kbp and therefore significantly larger than the previous estimates.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis.

claim: Around 15% of all transformants acquired and integrated more than 100 kbp.
source: Around 15% of all transformants acquired and integrated more than 100 kbp (Figure 3B), which was previously considered unlikely due to rareness of such long DNA fragments in the environment.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The new DNA was acquired through double homologous recombination such that it replaced the initial DNA region and the overall genome size did not significantly change.
source: Consistent with the principle of natural transformation, it should be noted that the new DNA was acquired through double homologous recombination such that it replaced the initial DNA region and the overall genome size did not significantly change.
evidence: This is an observation from the data consistent with the known mechanism of natural transformation.

claim: About 50% of the strains experienced a single HGT event around the aph cassette, while the others exchanged regions in up to eight different locations on the two chromosomes.
source: Further analysis indicated that about 50% of the strains experienced a single HGT event around the aph cassette, while the others exchanged regions in up to eight different locations on the two chromosomes (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The length of continuous DNA stretches acquired from the prey ranged from a few kbp up to 168 kbp.
source: Finally, we analyzed the length of continuous DNA stretches that were acquired from the prey and observed that those ranged from a few kbp up to 168 kbp (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: V. cholerae can acquire large genomic regions from killed neighbors with an average exchange of more than 50 kbp or ~50 genes.
source: Collectively, these data indicate that V. cholerae can acquire large genomic regions from killed neighbors with an average exchange of more than 50 kbp or ~50 genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The observed recombination events were significantly larger than the mean recombination event size of ~4 kbp recently reported for surface-grown Streptococcus pneumoniae.
source: Notably, our observed recombination events were significantly larger than the mean recombination event size of ~4 kbp that was recently reported for surface-grown Streptococcus pneumoniae (Cowley et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a comparison to previous research supported by citation.

claim: The findings contradict the notion that natural transformation is unlikely to serve DNA repair purposes or for the acquisition of new genetic information due to the quick fragmentation of free DNA in natural environments.
source: Their data combined with our findings therefore contradict the notion that natural transformation is unlikely to serve DNA repair purposes or for the acquisition of new genetic information due to the quick fragmentation of free DNA in natural environments (Nielsen et al., 2007; Overballe-Petersen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data in comparison to previous literature.

claim: When gDNA was added at the start of the chitin-dependent culture, no transformants were reproducibly detected from three independent biological experiments.
source: Notably, when the gDNA was added at the start of the chitin-dependent culture, no transformants were reproducibly detected from three independent biological experiments, suggesting that free DNA is rapidly degraded under such conditions.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding.

claim: Free DNA is rapidly degraded when added at the start of chitin-dependent culture.
source: Notably, when the gDNA was added at the start of the chitin-dependent culture, no transformants were reproducibly detected from three independent biological experiments, suggesting that free DNA is rapidly degraded under such conditions.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental observation of no transformants.

claim: V. cholerae produces an extracellular and periplasmic nuclease Dns that degrades transforming material.
source: This finding is consistent with our previous work in which we demonstrated that V. cholerae produces an extracellular and periplasmic nuclease Dns (Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2008; Seitz and Blokesch, 2014) that degrades transforming material.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research by the authors.

claim: At high cell density, dns is partially repressed through direct binding of HapR.
source: At high cell density (HCD), where competence is induced, dns is partially repressed through direct binding of HapR (Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2008; Lo Scrudato and Blokesch, 2013), and this repression is reinforced by the transcription factor QstR (Lo Scrudato and Blokesch, 2013; Jaskólska et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The simultaneous expression of both machineries (T6SS and DNA uptake), concomitantly with a strong repression of dns, is a prerequisite for successful DNA transfer.
source: We therefore concluded that the simultaneous expression of both machineries, concomitantly with a strong repression of dns, is a prerequisite for successful DNA transfer.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Coordinated expression of T6SS and DNA uptake ensures that T6SS-mediated attacks are exquisitely timed with low nuclease activity so that the prey-released DNA can be efficiently absorbed.
source: Indeed, such coordinated expression would ensure that T6SS-mediated attacks are exquisitely timed with low nuclease activity so that the prey-released DNA can be efficiently absorbed.
evidence: This is an inference about the mechanism based on the experimental observations.

claim: Adding purified gDNA after ~20–24 hr of growth on chitin led to similar transformation frequencies as those observed for the prey-released DNA caused by T6SS attacks.
source: As we previously showed that the addition of purified gDNA after ~20–24 hr of growth on chitin wasn't prone to degradation by Dns (Marvig and Blokesch, 2010), we next choose this time point to probe the DNA acquisition capability using purified DNA (condition ②; Figure 4A). Doing so led to similar transformation frequencies as those observed for the prey-released DNA caused by T6SS attacks (condition ①; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding supported by data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: WGS of transformants from condition ② resulted in similar DNA acquisition patterns with average and maximum DNA acquisitions of 70 kbp and 188 kbp, respectively.
source: WGS of 20 transformants from two biologically independent experiments likewise resulted in similar DNA acquisition patterns with average and maximum DNA acquisitions of 70 kbp and 188 kbp, respectively, and the presence of multiple exchanged regions of varying sizes (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: The maximum DNA acquisition length of single fragments is probably reached between 100–110 kbp.
source: While we cannot entirely exclude that the maximum length of individual DNA stretches was biased by the purification step, despite the fact that we chose a method that was designed for chromosomal DNA isolation of 20–150 kbp sized fragments (see Materials and methods), our results suggest that the maximum DNA acquisition length of single fragments is probably reached between 100–110 kbp (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the experimental data with acknowledgment of potential technical limitations.

claim: The comparable acquisition patterns between conditions ① and ② imply that the prey-released DNA in condition ① is neither heavily fragmented nor is its accessibility or absorption significantly hindered.
source: Moreover, the comparable acquisition patterns between conditions ① and ② (Figure 4) imply that the prey-released DNA in condition ① is neither heavily fragmented nor is its accessibility or absorption by the competent acceptor bacterium significantly hindered due to, for example, DNA-binding proteins.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the comparison of experimental conditions.

claim: Similar transformation frequencies were observed independent of the position of the aph cassette.
source: Since the aph cassette was located within the T6SS sheath protein gene vipA in the above experiments, we wondered if this T6SS inactivation biased the DNA transfer efficiency. We therefore repeated the above-described experiments using prey strains that carried the aph cassette on the opposite site of chr 2 (within gene VCA0747; condition ③). As shown in (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), similar transformation frequencies were observed independent of the position of the aph cassette.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: WGS of transformants from condition ③ showed similar average and maximum DNA acquisition values (55.7 kbp and 227.4 kbp, respectively).
source: Moreover, WGS of 2 × 20 transformants showed similar average and maximum DNA acquisition values (55.7 kbp and 227.4 kbp, respectively; Figure 4) as well as similar distribution patterns around the resistance marker (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: Transformants with only single/connected exchanges dropped from ~50% in condition ① to around 20% in condition ③.
source: However, while not statistically supported, it appeared as if these conditions were prone to the acquisition of multiple non-connected regions, as transformants with only single/connected exchanges dropped from ~50% (Figure 4—figure supplement 2 for condition ①) to around 20% (Figure 4—figure supplement 4 for condition ③).
evidence: This is an observation from the data, though not statistically significant.

claim: The restored T6SS-mediated killing capacity of the prey may lead to additional release of genomic DNA from the predator, which interferes with the uptake of prey-released DNA.
source: Based on this observation, we hypothesized that the now-restored T6SS-mediated killing capacity of the prey led to the additional release of genomic DNA from the predator, which interfered with the uptake of prey-released DNA.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the experimental observations.

claim: No statistically significant differences were observed between conditions ③ and ④ for all tested characteristics including transformation frequency, number of exchanges, and separate and collective length.
source: No statistically significant differences were observed between both conditions (③ and ④) for all tested characteristics including transformation frequency (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), number of exchanges, and separate and collective length (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplements 4 and 5), suggesting that predator-released DNA does not interfere with the predator's overall transformability by the prey-released DNA.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from statistical analysis of the data.

claim: Predator-released DNA does not interfere with the predator's overall transformability by the prey-released DNA.
source: No statistically significant differences were observed between both conditions (③ and ④) for all tested characteristics including transformation frequency (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), number of exchanges, and separate and collective length (Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplements 4 and 5), suggesting that predator-released DNA does not interfere with the predator's overall transformability by the prey-released DNA.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the lack of statistical differences between conditions.

claim: When both donor and acceptor strains were T6SS-defective, the transformation frequency dropped by 99.7%.
source: We next tested whether T6SS-mediated DNA release impacted the length of the exchanged region, which would support the above speculation that the intimate co-regulation of type VI secretion, nuclease repression, and DNA uptake ensures that freshly released DNA is rapidly absorbed by the predator and is therefore less prone to fragmentation. Such co-regulation would not hold true for T6SS-independent DNA release as a result of random cell lysis, so we tested the transfer efficiency of the aph cassette under conditions in which both donor and acceptor strains were T6SS-defective (condition ⑤; Figure 4 and Figure 4—figure supplement 6). Under such conditions, the transformation frequency dropped by 99.7% (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), and WGS of 2 × 20 of these rare transformants showed significant differences.
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The average and maximal length of acquired DNA and the number of exchanged regions were significantly different when T6SS+ versus T6SS- acceptor strains were compared.
source: Indeed, the average and maximal length of acquired DNA (Figure 4B) and the number of exchanged regions (Figure 4C) were significantly different when T6SS+ versus T6SS- acceptor strains were compared, with the latter exchanges never exceeding four events compared to up to 13 events for T6SS-mediated DNA release (Figure 4—figure supplements 5 and 6).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding from statistical analysis shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: T6SS-mediated DNA acquisition increases the transfer efficiency by ~100 fold and fosters the exchange of multiple DNA stretches of extended lengths.
source: Based on these data, we conclude that T6SS-mediated DNA acquisition not only increases the transfer efficiency by ~100 fold but also fosters the exchange of multiple DNA stretches of extended lengths.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing T6SS+ and T6SS- conditions.

claim: Comparing conditions ⑥ (co-culture conditions) and ⑧ (prey-derived purified gDNA) revealed a small but significant transformation increase for the latter condition (~4 fold).
source: As shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1, the aph cassette was again transferred with high efficiency from the killed prey strain to the acceptor strain. However, comparing conditions ⑥ (co-culture conditions) and ⑧ (prey-derived purified gDNA as transforming material) revealed a small but significant transformation increase for the latter condition (~4 fold; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The larger size of chr 1 (~3 Mb) compared to chr 2 (~1 Mb) slightly lowers the probability of acquiring the aph cassette when released from the killed prey that carried the resistance marker on chr 1.
source: Based on these data, we speculate that the larger size of chr 1 (~3 Mb) compared to chr 2 (~1 Mb) slightly lowers the probability of acquiring the aph cassette when released from the killed prey that carried the resistance marker on chr 1.
evidence: This is speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: The cassette's relative occupancy per chromosome is reduced by one third for the larger chromosome 1 compared to the smaller chromosome 2.
source: Indeed, the cassette's relative occupancy per chromosome is reduced by one third for the larger chromosome 1 compared to the smaller chromosome 2, which would reduce the chance of absorbing the aph cassette if it was embedded in large chromosomal fragment(s).
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the relative sizes of the chromosomes.

claim: Purified gDNA from all prey strains resulted in the same level of transformation no matter where the selective marker was located.
source: Consistent with this idea was the finding that purified gDNA from all those prey strains described in this study resulted in the same level of transformation no matter where the selective marker was located (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a primary experimental finding shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claim: The average and maximum DNA acquisition values for transformants with markers on chromosome 1 were highly comparable to those for DNA exchanges on chromosome 2.
source: Next, we randomly picked 20 transformants from two biologically independent experiments for each of these three experimental conditions (⑥ to ⑧) and sequenced their genomes (Figure 4—figure supplements 7 to 9). The analysis of these transformants showed that the average and maximum DNA acquisition values were highly comparable to those described above for DNA exchanges on chromosome 2 (Figure 4B) and that multiple exchanged regions were likewise observed (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the whole-genome sequencing analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Prey-derived transforming DNA can equally modify both chromosomes.
source: We therefore conclude that prey-derived transforming DNA can equally modify both chromosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing transformations on both chromosomes.

claim: Consecutive stretches of exchanged DNA above ~200 kbp either do not occur or occur at levels below the detection limit of this study.
source: Moreover, our data suggest that consecutive stretches of exchanged DNA above ~200 kbp either do not occur or occur at levels below the detection limit of this study, and that this size limitation is not caused by the toxin/antitoxin–module-containing integron island on chr 2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: The size limitation of DNA transfer is not caused by the toxin/antitoxin–module-containing integron island on chr 2.
source: Moreover, our data suggest that consecutive stretches of exchanged DNA above ~200 kbp either do not occur or occur at levels below the detection limit of this study, and that this size limitation is not caused by the toxin/antitoxin–module-containing integron island on chr 2.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data comparing both chromosomes.

claim: T6SS-mediated predation followed by DNA uptake leads to the exchange of large DNA regions that can bring about bacterial evolution.
source: Based on the data presented above, we conclude that T6SS-mediated predation followed by DNA uptake leads to the exchange of large DNA regions that can bring about bacterial evolution.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented.

claim: Heterogeneous environmental V. cholerae populations were observed in cholera-endemic areas.
source: This finding is consistent with the heterogeneous environmental V. cholerae populations that were observed in cholera-endemic areas (Faruque et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: Pandemic cholera isolates are seemingly clonal in nature.
source: Still, an open question that remains is why pandemic cholera isolates are seemingly clonal in nature (Mutreja et al., 2011; Domman et al., 2017; Weill et al., 2017; Weill et al., 2019), and we propose two explanations for this.
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous research.

claim: Sampling strategies might be biased for the selection of the most pathogenic strains and exclude less virulent variants that have undergone HGT events.
source: First, sampling strategies might be biased for the selection of the most pathogenic strains and, concomitantly, exclude less virulent variants that have undergone HGT events.
evidence: This is speculation about potential sampling bias.

claim: Transformation-inhibiting nucleases similar to Dns have recently spread throughout pandemic V. cholerae isolates as part of mobile genetic elements.
source: Secondly, transformation-inhibiting nucleases similar to Dns (Blokesch and Schoolnik, 2008) have recently spread throughout pandemic V. cholerae isolates as part of mobile genetic elements (experimentally shown for VchInd5 [Dalia et al., 2015] and predicted for SXT [Blokesch, 2017]), which makes these pandemic strains less likely to undergo HGT events.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: IVIAT assays showed strong human immune responses against proteins of the DNA-uptake pilus.
source: Yet in vivo-induced antigen technology (IVIAT) assays showed strong human immune responses against proteins of the DNA-uptake pilus that fosters natural transformation, kin recognition, and chitin colonization (Meibom et al., 2005; Seitz and Blokesch, 2013; Adams et al., 2019), which contradicts this idea.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous research.

claim: The major pilin of the DNA-uptake pilus, PilA, was most frequently identified by IVIAT together with the outer-membrane secretin PilQ.
source: Indeed, the major pilin of the DNA-uptake pilus, PilA, was most frequently identified by IVIAT together with the outer-membrane secretin PilQ (Hang et al., 2003), which suggests that the bacteria encounter competence-inducing conditions either before entering the human host or after its colonization.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The bacteria encounter competence-inducing conditions either before entering the human host or after its colonization.
source: Indeed, the major pilin of the DNA-uptake pilus, PilA, was most frequently identified by IVIAT together with the outer-membrane secretin PilQ (Hang et al., 2003), which suggests that the bacteria encounter competence-inducing conditions either before entering the human host or after its colonization.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the IVIAT data.

claim: In vivo expression data from human volunteers does not support the idea that bacteria encounter competence-inducing conditions after colonization.
source: The latter option is not, however, supported by in vivo expression data from human volunteers (Lombardo et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous research.

claim: The work shows the incredible DNA exchange potential that chitin-induced V. cholerae strains exert under co-culture conditions.
source: Notably, our work shows the incredible DNA exchange potential that chitin-induced V. cholerae strains exert under co-culture conditions and future studies are therefore required to better understand strain diversity in clinical and environmental settings in the absence of sampling biases.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.
